hook.text: Your app has 20 microservices. Does the mobile app need to know all 20 addresses? An API gateway says no.

buildup.text: An API gateway is a single entry point that routes requests to the right service behind the scenes.

discovery.text: It also handles authentication, rate limiting, and caching — so individual services don't have to.

twist.text: The gateway becomes a single point of failure. If it goes down, nothing behind it is reachable.

climax.text: Cloud-managed gateways like AWS API Gateway and Azure API Management reduce that risk with built-in redundancy.

punchline.text: One door in. Many services behind. That's the gateway.

quiz.question: What is the role of an API gateway in microservices?
options: A single entry point that routes requests and handles cross-cutting concerns
A database that stores all API documentation
A tool that automatically generates microservice code

details.summary: An API gateway is a single entry point that routes client requests to appropriate backend services. It handles cross-cutting concerns like authentication, rate limiting, logging, and response transformation, so individual services do not have to.
details.whyItMatters: API gateways simplify client integration and centralize security enforcement. They are essential in microservices architectures where clients would otherwise need to know about dozens of service endpoints.
takeaways: Provides a single entry point for all client requests
Handles auth, rate limiting, and logging centrally
Decouples clients from backend service topology

faq.question: What is the difference between an API gateway and a load balancer?
faq.answer: A load balancer distributes traffic across instances of the same service. An API gateway routes requests to different services based on the request path or content, and adds cross-cutting features like auth and transformation. They often work together.

faq.question: Can an API gateway become a bottleneck?
faq.answer: Yes. Since all traffic flows through it, the gateway must be highly available and horizontally scalable. Managed services like AWS API Gateway and Azure API Management handle scaling automatically. Self-hosted gateways need careful capacity planning.
